newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Italian wins award with photo of Angolan children.
newsitem.headline: Italian wins award with photo of Angolan children.

text.p: Francesco Zizola of Italian photo bureau Agenzia Contrasto won the 1996 World Press Photo of the Year award on Friday with his emotion-charged image of children traumatised by the Angolan civil war.
His April 1996 photograph shows a girl clutching a doll while a boy with one leg balances on his crutches at a centre for children in the city of Quito.
Many children have been maimed by land mines during the war in the southern African country.
Zizola, a previous winner of category awards in the competition, is the first Italian to win the World Press Photo of the Year award, held for the 40th time in 1996.
Among the other winners were Reuters' U.S. photographers Corinne Dufka, first for "spot news stories", and Stephen Jaffe, who won the "people in the news" category.
A record 3,663 photographers from 119 countries submitted 36,650 entries.
An international jury selected winners from 18 categories ranging from natural disasters to sports.
An exhibition of the best photos from the contest opens in Amsterdam on April 28.
